senses.definition: Made of separate systems that keep their own data and rules but work together as one.
senses.caution: Say what stays separate, such as data or logins, because people use the word in different ways.
senses.example: We use federated login, so staff sign in once with their company account and every tool trusts it.

cues.text: Each hospital keeps its patient records on site, but a shared model learns from all of them without the records ever leaving.
You explain a search page that queries five databases, each owned by a different team, and shows one list of results.

Staff sign in with their company account, and a dozen outside tools, each run by a different vendor with its own rules, agree to trust that one login. You want the adjective for this kind of identity setup.
You explain how a social network lets people on different servers, each run by different volunteers, follow each other.

distractors: Stored in one central place that every team reads from.
Locked so that only one person can change it at a time.
Copied in full to every server so that nothing is lost.
Built by an outside company and rented by the month, so that nobody in the team has to run it.
Moved from an old platform to a new one in small steps, so that users do not notice any change at all.

gloss_distractors: ruled directly by a foreign power
senses.definition: Joined with others under one central government, while each keeps some power of its own.
senses.caution: It is a formal word from politics, law, and history. Name the parts that joined, such as states or provinces, so the meaning is clear.
senses.example: The provinces are federated, so each one sets its own school rules but they all share one army.

cues.text: You brief a client that each state in a country sets its own tax rules, while the national government handles defence and trade.
In a memo on entering a new country, you describe how its provinces keep their own laws under one central government.
A history podcast explains how several small kingdoms agreed to share one army and one currency but keep their own rulers.

distractors: Ruled by a single leader who holds all power.
Split into two countries after a long dispute over land.
Governed directly by a distant foreign country that took control of it by force many years ago.
Free from any central government, with each town making every one of its own laws without outside say.
